MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  FEBRUARY 19, 2025

1.  CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall
  Council Chamber.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Brown Schachter, Combs, Halvorsen, Hall
  Munday, Olson, Rowe, Tertzakian

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Martin, Nash, Persichina

  ALSO PRESENT:  Deputy Duran, LACSD

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Public Works Director
  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Jessica Slawson, Assistant to the City Manager
  Reggie Greene, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, NOVEMBER
  20, 2024.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
MUNDAY to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  NOVEMBER 20, 2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  E-BIKE POLICY – VERBAL UPDATE

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson stated that the City has a working group on e-bikes with
the other cities on the Peninsula and a partnership with the School District and the South Bay
Cities Council of Governments. They meet quarterly to discuss e-bike safety; Rolling Hills Estates
is focused on e-bike safety education. The Lomita Sheriff’s Stations Community Relations Division
has done numerous PSA’s, pamphlets, and attended PTA meetings to discuss e-bike education.
Assistant to the City Manager Slawson stated that they are hoping to expand a pilot program for
e-bike registration with the school district in order to enforce rules of the road and safety. Staff is
keeping an eye on any new legislation and has met with Assembly Member Muratsuchi’s office
on any proposed Statewide legislation. There were new laws that came into effect January 1 that
were related to the manufacturing of e-bikes.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE asked if registration is only of the e-bike and not the individual
riding the e-bike. Assistant to the City Manager Slawson stated that it is both the e-bike and the
individual. Ridgecrest Intermediate is the school participating in the program and is working with
the Community Relations team at the Sheriff’s Department. If there are issues, then the
registration is revoked and the student is no longer allowed to bring the e-bike to the school. In
order to reinstate the registration, the student would need to complete an e-bike safety course.

CHAIR SCHACHTER asked about the various speed levels that are allowed. Assistant to the City
Manager Slawson stated that there was legislation introduced on the top speed; however, it is for
the manufacturer.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, February 19, 2025
 Deputy Duran stated that the focus is more on education than enforcement. There are issues with
the Surron bikes, which are much faster than e-bikes. He stated that they are doing their best on
the enforcement side; however, education is the focus. Parents are not aware of what they are
buying their kids, and believe they are buying e-bikes where in reality it is a electric motorcycle.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that Mike Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent, had a-
frames made with information of where e-bikes are prohibited, and they are moved to different
trails or school entrances around the City.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN asked where the biggest issues are with e-bikes when it
pertains to age demographic. Assistant to the City Manager Slawson stated that it is mostly with
middle school aged students.

B.1. DEEP VALLEY DRIVE CROSSWALK AND BULB-OUT AT LIBRARY/KUMON LEARNING
  CENTER

Director Wahba provided a presentation summarizing the staff report on the various options for
the location of the crosswalk and bulb-out on Deep Valley Drive between the PVP Library and
Kumon Learning Center (627 Deep Valley Drive). He provided background on the paving,
crosswalk, and pedestrian improvement project in the City. Director Wahba noted that when
reviewing this project for the crosswalk options, the preliminary plans for the project at 655 Deep
Valley Drive show a discrepancy with the proposed crosswalk and the location of the proposed
driveway; this will need to be communicated to the applicant in order to revise their plans.

Director Wahba provides the following three options:

  1. Crosswalk in front of existing fire hydrant/red curb. This will include a bulb-out that will
  narrow the street, as well as solar powered flashing lights, which will help calm traffic. A
  total of four parking spaces will be lost, two parking spaces on the north and south sides
  of the street. There is legislation that requires 15 FT clearance from the crosswalk.

  2. Crosswalk in front of Kumon Learning Center, which is further from the traffic circle and
  provides better spacing between crosswalks. A total of six parking spaces will be lost with
  this option and only one parking space in front of 627 Deep Valley Drive.

  3. Crosswalk in front of the PVP Library (original design), which has an existing bulb-out that
  would be extended for the crosswalk.

The recommendation from the Traffic and Safety Committee will be presented to the City Council
at its meeting on February 25 and begin the engineering for this project and begin the project in
the summer.

Director Wahba stated that the overall project design included a crosswalk in front of the 927
Deep Valley Drive project; however, after further review with Willdan and the curve in the road it
was determined to remove the crosswalk from the design.

COMMITTEE MUNDAY requested clarification on the loss of parking spaces due to the bulb-out
in option 1. Director Wahba explained that the code requires 15 FT clearance from the crosswalk.
Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene further explained the required distance from the crosswalk
due to the installation of the bulb-out.

A discussion ensued on the various options.

Director Naughton provided clarification regarding The Village parking adjacent to the library and
stated that there is a reciprocal agreement and overflow parking for the library is available on the
top deck of the parking structure. Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that the rules do not
change.

Dan Houk, La Collina HOA, stated that he favors options 1 and 2; however, the option with the
least amount of parking loss would be preferable.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, February 19, 2025
 Kaia Shimitu, Reverent Coffee Owner, stated that the issue is that no matter what, people will still
park in the red no parking zone. Parents of children picking up their kids park in the red zone for
hours and it is not being enforced. Director Wahba stated that the bulb-out should help. She stated
that she has spoken to various agencies about this issue and stated that it is dangerous for
pedestrians to cross due to the limited visibility with the cars parked in the red zone.

Ms. Shimitu asked if there will be in-ground solar powered flashers. Director Wahba stated that it
would have to be electrified and due to the cost it will only be the solar-powered flashing beacons
on the signs.

Dante Marrocco, Resident 627 Deep Valley Drive, stated that the red zone is not wide enough;
he stated that if a vehicle is parked where they are not supposed to, exiting the driveway is
dangerous. Mr. Marrocco stated that he prefers option 1 and asked if there was consideration to
angle the crosswalk to possible save a parking space. Mr. Marrocco expressed his appreciation
for considering this item.

Mr. Houk stated that he has spoken to the owner of Kumon Learning Center and has put signs
out to discourage parking in the red zone and is actively trying to get parents to stop doing this.

Ms. Shimitu stated that the owner of Kumon has placed cones out on the street and they are
removed and people continue to park in the red zone. She added that the child who was recently
hit crossing the street was a student of his, so this issue is important to him.

COMMITTEE MUNDAY asked if it is necessary to have two lanes around the traffic circle. Director
Wahba stated that it was designed this way in the late 90’s to make it efficient for traffic flow.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY asked if the rules change (for parking distance from the
crosswalk) if the parking space is for a limited amount of time.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE asked where people are parking if they are not parking on the
street. Mr. Houk and Ms. Shimitu confirmed that they will typically parking in the upper deck
parking structure.

CHAIR SCHACHTER asked about parking enforcement. Deputy Duran stated that he and Deputy
Clotworthy has issued at least four dozen tickets each in this area.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN suggested placing a physical barrier, such as extending
the bulb-out or installing planters, in the street in front of the no parking areas. Director Wahba
stated that staff can look into extending the bulb-out.

COMMITTEE MEMBER TERTZAKIAN asked if outside of the parking spaces, has safety
consideration such as speed from the traffic circle. Director Wahba stated that coming out of the
traffic circle and seeing the crosswalk tends to make people slow down; however, crosswalks
should have sufficient distance between each other. Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene added
that utilities and trees are taken into consideration when determining where to place crosswalks.

Ms. Shimitu suggested considering bike racks in addition to planters.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE inquired about funding for the project. Director Wahba stated that
most is being funded by the City and a Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) grant for
$250K. The total of the project is approximately $1.5M.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE expressed his concern with the location of Kumon Learning
Center and if anything could be done to relocate them. Director Wahba stated that this item
(crosswalk being discussed) is part of a larger improvement project.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN stated that option 2 is in front of Kumon, which seems to
be where the bigger issue is in this area. Director Wahba stated that this option would lose more
parking spaces.

COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
TERTZAKIAN to,

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  3
Minutes, February 19, 2025
   A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO ACCEPT OPTION 1 FOR THE
  CROSSWALK LOCATION; EXTEND THE BULB-OUT ON THE SOUTH TO PREVENT
  VEHICLES FROM PARKING IN THE RED ZONE; AND, TO INSTALL BIKE RACKS OR
  PLANTERS IN THAT AREA AS DETERMINED BY STAFF; AND, TO ACCOMMODATE
  ONE PARKING SPACE IN FRONT OF 627 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE IF FEASIBLE.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Combs, Halvorsen, Hall Munday, Olson, Rowe, Tertzakian
NOES:
ABSENT: Martin, Nash, Persichina
ABSTAIN:

B.2. PVDN TRAFFIC AND SIGNAL TIMING RESULTS

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene provided a presentation with a summary of the staff report on
the traffic and signal timing results. The average daily traffic (ADT) on PVDN is approximately
8,000 – 16,000 vehicles per day; 3,500 vehicles per day on Rolling Hills Road; the highest volume
is on Rolling Hills Road/PVDN. The traffic demand during school peak hours exceeds the
available capacity and the traffic signal timing is optimal to balance the demand. The congestion
cannot be significantly improved with timing modifications. Other than widening the street, there
is no other solution to resolve congestion. Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene provided historical
data on the traffic flow and signal timing study on PVDN and it showed that the ADT went down
between 2014 and 2021, likely due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The ADT remained steady from
2021 to 2024. The 85th percentile speed has remained relatively steady; and the reported
collisions are below the expected rate.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER noted that there was an increase in ADT on Rolling Hills Road
and Palos Verdes Drive North in 2006 and stated that she would like to know when Dapplegray
became an elementary school, which may be a reason for the increase.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that during peak hours (approx. 6pm) the signal from
London Lane onto PVDN is triggered from vehicles coming from Dapplegray School and asked if
the signal changes depending on the time of day. Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that
it changes depending on the time of day and traffic flow.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that he believes the biggest issue is the vehicles coming
out from the school because the bottleneck occurs up to Rolling Hills Road.

COMMITTEE MEMBER TERTZAKIAN stated that she turns left at the London Lane signal at
about that time and waits for a while for the light to turn and will pay closer attention to what
happens at that signal.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that the light is triggered when making a left; if someone
stops and leaves (turning right), the light is not triggered.

Lynne Yen, Resident, stated that the school district may be considering changing the elementary
school to one pick-up time and the data may change since more people may carpool and the use
of private or tutoring center buses. The traffic may also be due to the different pick-up times and
parents having to loop around multiple times to pick up their children.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene shared a few videos of the various intersections; he concluded
that timing modifications would not make a considerable improvement to traffic.

The Committee Members requested to see videos that were recorded later in the afternoons.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALL stated that there seems to be a lot of traffic a few minutes after
8:00 a.m. hour since parents are often running late than those that are on time.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER asked how much time it takes for parents to drop off. COMMITTEE
MEMBER COMBS stated that the school has people on duty trying to push people along.

Director Wahba stated that the recommendation is to receive and file this report.

B.3. SPEED LIMIT DISCUSSION ON PVDN (ASSEMBLY BILL 43)

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  4
Minutes, February 19, 2025
 Director Wahba stated that the speed limit is 35 MPH west of Hawthorne Blvd. to the Palos Verdes
Estates city limit; the speed limit from Hawthorne Blvd. to Palos Verdes Drive East is 40 MPH;
and, the speed limit from Palos Verdes Drive East to the Lomita city limit is 45 MPH.

Director Wahba stated that the request here is whether the speed limit from east of Hawthorne
Blvd. to Palos Verdes Drive East should be changed to 35 MPH to be consistent to what the limit
is on the rest of PVDN and through Palos Verdes Estates.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that Assembly Bill 43 was introduced in 2022 and has
been implemented and there are provisions to allow this to happen. In order to meet the guidelines
for the 5 MPH reduction, there must be a designated safety corridor or there must be a designation
of land uses or facilities with a high concentration generator of bicyclists or pedestrians. It is
unclear how cities need to verify either of these, and more research should be done prior to
making any changes. Director Wahba stated that the question for the committee is whether to
direct Willdan to begin doing a study on this item.

COMMITTEE MEMBER TERTZAKIAN asked when the last Traffic Survey was done. Traffic
Engineering Deputy Greene stated that it was in 2021.

COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON asked what the cost of the study would be. Traffic Engineering
Deputy Greene stated that it would not be too expensive.

A brief discussion ensued.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALL made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON to,

  DIRECT STAFF TO CONDUCT A STUDY TO VERIFY IF THE CITY MEETS THE
  GUIDELINES TO REDUCE THE SPEED LIMIT ON PVDN BY 5 MPH.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Combs, Halvorsen, Hall Munday, Olson, Rowe, Tertzakian
NOES:
ABSENT: Martin, Nash, Persichina
ABSTAIN:

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

Item taken out of order
4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

Lynne Yen, Resident asked if the disabled ramp from the George F Canyon Nature Center is
intended for vehicles to come in and stated that there is a lot of activity in that area and asked if
an a-frame could be placed there if that is not the intention. Director Wahba stated that he can
work with Ms. Yen on this issue administratively.

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN stated that some of the streetlights are out at the
intersection of PVDN & PVDE, and it is very dark on the south side of Palos Verdes Drive East.
Director Wahba stated that he can reach out to SCE.

COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON stated that the guardrail on Silver Spur Road when travelling
north from PVDN is constantly being hit and asked if anything could be done. Director Wahba
stated that this has been reviewed and a new guardrail with larger cap and signs were installed.
The last accident was a DUI.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY asked about the city’s evacuation plans in case of a fire and
coordination with the other cities. Director Wahba stated that this is being worked on in
coordination with the other cities on the Peninsula. Director Naughton stated that the City currently
has a Joint Hazard Mitigation Plan with the City of Rancho Palos Verdes and now the City is at
the MOU stage and the City will work with the other three cities on the Peninsula to enable a
citywide focus on evacuation. There is some uncertainty in regard to federal funding to prepare
the plan. Assuming that there is funding, the project will be done in the next year. A good resource
to look into is “Know Your Zone” which can be found on the City’s website.
